compliance_rules.description: Arkmurus requires a SITEL (Standard Individual Trade Control Licence) for each brokering deal arranging transfer of controlled military goods between two overseas countries. Apply via SPIRE (spire.trade.gov.uk).

End User Certificate must be obtained from the buying government BEFORE applying for any export or brokering licence. Must include: full legal name/address, ML classification, quantity, specific end use, non-re-export clause, authorised official signature and stamp.

Any item containing US-origin ITAR-controlled components remains ITAR-controlled regardless of where manufactured or integrated. Arkmurus must check every deal for US-origin content. Zero de minimis threshold.

Arms Trade Treaty Article 7 requires risk assessment before authorising any export. If overriding risk that arms could undermine peace/security, violate IHL, or violate human rights law, the export SHALL NOT be authorised.

Under Section 7 of the UK Bribery Act 2010, Arkmurus can be criminally liable for failing to prevent bribery by associated persons. Strict liability offence — defence is proving adequate procedures were in place.
UK brokering controls under Trade in Goods (Control) Order 2003 are extraterritorial — they apply to UK persons anywhere in the world. Arkmurus staff must comply regardless of physical location.

Both ATT and UK export control legislation require maintaining records of all authorised transfers for minimum 10 years. Retain all EUCs, licence applications, correspondence, and transaction records.

Before any engagement, screen all parties against: UN consolidated list, EU sanctions list, UK OFSI sanctions list, US OFAC SDN list, BIS Entity List, and any country-specific lists relevant to the transaction.

All UK export licence decisions assessed against 8 Consolidated Criteria: (1) International obligations, (2) Human rights, (3) Internal situation, (4) Regional stability, (5) National security, (6) Buyer behaviour, (7) Diversion risk, (8) Economic capacity.
EU Regulation 2021/821 governs dual-use exports. Catch-all provision (Article 4) can control non-listed items if exporter is aware of WMD/military end-use. Member states issue licences independently.

US ITAR Part 129 requires all brokers of USML items to register with DDTC and obtain per-transaction DSP-5 approval. Applies to US persons AND foreign persons if US-origin items involved. Penalties up to $1M and 20 years.

ATT Article 11 requires measures to prevent diversion. Risk assessment, mitigation measures, and cooperation on diversion cases mandatory. Red flags include: vague end-use, routing anomalies, capability mismatch, multiple intermediaries.
